prompt: Analyze Salesforce CRM data by discovering schema, running SOQL queries, extracting a large set of related records, and computing a cohort-based return-rate metric.

results.use_case: Analyze Salesforce CRM data by discovering schema, running SOQL queries, extracting a large set of related records, and computing a cohort-based return-rate metric.
results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if fields/relationships uncertain)] [Prerequisite]: Inspect object schema using SALESFORCE_GET_ALL_FIELDS_FOR_OBJECT (confirm queryable fields before writing large SELECTs).
[Required] [Step]: Run the base SOQL using SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY (capture data.done, data.totalSize, and data.nextRecordsUrl for paging state).

[Required (if data.nextRecordsUrl present)] [Next Step]: Page through REST query pages using COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH (GET each nextRecordsUrl, append data.records, stop when done=true and nextRecordsUrl is null).
[Optional (if soft-deleted/archived rows must be included)] [Step]: Re-run the same SOQL via SALESFORCE_QUERY_ALL (then page identically if nextRecordsUrl is returned).

[Optional (if a Bulk API v2 query job already exists for the SOQL)] [Next Step]: Stream results in chunks using SALESFORCE_GET_QUERY_JOB_RESULTS (pass locator/maxRecords forward until the response stops returning locator).

[Optional (if a query job should not persist)] [Next Step]: Verify state using SALESFORCE_GET_QUERY_JOB_INFO, then end or remove it using SALESFORCE_CLOSE_OR_ABORT_JOB or SALESFORCE_DELETE_JOB_QUERY (avoid lingering jobs).
known_pitfalls: [SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY] nextRecordsUrl can 404 if requested in an incompatible form; prefer requesting the returned /query/... path rather than rewriting it to a version-prefixed URL.
[SALESFORCE_GET_QUERY_JOB_RESULTS] Continue only while a locator is returned; dropping/ignoring locator can skip rows or cause accidental loops.
[SALESFORCE_QUERY_ALL] Includes soft-deleted/archived rows that SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY excludes, so counts and analysis outputs can differ.
[SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY] Query responses may nest rows under data.records (don’t assume a top-level records array).
[SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY] Large IN-clause filtering can exceed practical query size; chunk identifiers into smaller batches to avoid oversized queries.

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Minimal loop to follow nextRecordsUrl pages (normalize to the /query/... path) and accumulate data.records via COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH calls.
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
def norm(u):
    if not u: return None
    return u.split('/query',1)[-1].join(['','/query']) if '/query' in u and not u.startswith('/query') else u
first=sf_query(soql)['data']
rows=list(first.get('records') or [])
nu=norm(first.get('nextRecordsUrl'))
while nu:
    page=sf_get(nu)
    rows+=list(page.get('records') or [])
    nu=norm(page.get('nextRecordsUrl'))
```

SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY.description: Executes a SOQL query against Salesforce data. Returns records matching the query with pagination support.

examples: SELECT Id, Name, Email FROM Contact WHERE CreatedDate > 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z
SELECT Name, (SELECT LastName FROM Contacts) FROM Account
SELECT COUNT() FROM Lead WHERE Status = 'New'
SELECT COUNT(Id), StageName FROM Opportunity GROUP BY StageName
SELECT Id, Name FROM Opportunity ORDER BY Amount DESC LIMIT 10
SELECT Id, Name FROM Contact WHERE LastName = 'O\'Brien'
SELECT Id, Name, Description FROM Account LIMIT 10
query.description: SOQL query to execute. Must start with SELECT. Field names must match object schema exactly — use SALESFORCE_GET_ALL_FIELDS_FOR_OBJECT for unfamiliar objects. ALIASES: No 'AS' keyword (use 'SUM(Amount) TotalSales' NOT 'SUM(Amount) AS TotalSales'). AGGREGATES: Without GROUP BY, ORDER BY/LIMIT not allowed (single-row result). COUNT() SYNTAX: Bare COUNT() only valid alone. With GROUP BY or other fields, must specify field: COUNT(Id) or COUNT(fieldName). Example: 'SELECT COUNT(Id), Status FROM Lead GROUP BY Status' NOT 'SELECT COUNT(), Status FROM Lead GROUP BY Status'. NON-GROUPABLE: Long text, rich text, encrypted text, compound address/location fields. NON-FILTERABLE: Long text area, rich text, encrypted text, multi-select picklists, blob fields CANNOT be in WHERE. FIELDS(ALL)/FIELDS(CUSTOM) require LIMIT ≤200. ID values need single quotes. Apostrophes use backslash: 'O\'Brien'.

SALESFORCE_GET_QUERY_JOB_RESULTS.description: Retrieves results for a completed Bulk API v2 query job in CSV format. Supports pagination for large datasets via maxRecords and locator parameters.

job_id.description: The unique 18-character identifier for the query job whose results you want to retrieve.

locator.description: A Base64-encoded string used for pagination to retrieve the next set of records. This value is obtained from the Sforce-Locator response header of the previous request. Use this to traverse through subsequent pages of results.

max_records.description: Defines the number of records to be downloaded per page. If omitted, the API returns the maximum number of records it can send in a single page. Used to control page size for pagination.

SALESFORCE_GET_ALL_FIELDS_FOR_OBJECT.description: Retrieves all fields (standard and custom) for a Salesforce object with complete metadata including field types, constraints, picklist values, and relationships.

object_name.description: API name of the Salesforce object to describe. Use standard object names (Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity) or custom object API names ending in __c.
